slides.say: A number leaves a remainder of four when divided by five. Which of the following expressions could represent the number? x is an integer.

So we know the remainder by five, and every choice is an expression with x. Remember, a number that leaves four when divided by five is five k plus four, full fives plus four. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, splitting off the fives in each choice, and then plugging in a number.

[short pause] Let's start by splitting off the fives. In each choice, the part that divides by five doesn't matter, and only what's left decides. Choice number one, five x plus seven. Five x is always full fives. Seven is one five plus two, so it leaves two, not four. Out.

Choice number two, five x plus two, squared. Let's open it with the formula, a plus b, squared. Five x squared is twenty-five x squared, two times five x times two is twenty x, and two squared is four.
Twenty-five x squared and twenty x both divide by five, and what's left is four. That's exactly the remainder we need, so choice number two is our answer.
at: choice number two is our answer

slides.say: And here's a shortcut for next time. Everything built from five x divides by five too, so I only need the square of the number at the end, two squared, four.

In the exam you'd circle it and move on. Here, the other two with the shortcut. Ten x plus eight. Ten x is full fives, and eight is one five plus three. Out. Five x plus five, squared. The last number is five, and five squared is twenty-five, exactly five fives, nothing left. Out.

[pause] Now let's try plugging in a number. x is any integer, so I'll take zero. Why zero? Here every choice leaves the same remainder for every x, because the x part is always full fives. So the easiest number is the best.
at: the x part is always full fives

slides.say: With x zero, the choices are seven, two squared, which is four, eight, and five squared, which is twenty-five.
Divided by five, seven leaves two, four leaves four, eight leaves three, and twenty-five leaves nothing. Only four leaves four, so choice number two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
